question: A non-rebreather mask (NRM) with high-flow oxygen can deliver a FiO₂ of approximately 60–90%, making it the highest-FiO₂ device available without invasive ventilation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The NRM at high-flow rates delivers ~60–90% FiO₂. This makes it the device of choice for a severely hypoxic child who can maintain spontaneous breathing. Compare: nasal cannula ~24–44%, simple mask ~40–60%, Venturi mask = fixed FiO₂ by adapter (precise but not as high).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A properly fitted NRM at 10–15 L/min delivers ~60–90% FiO₂, the highest of all non-invasive oxygen delivery devices. By contrast: nasal cannula ~24–44% (1–6 L/min), simple mask ~40–60%, and Venturi mask delivers a FIXED precise FiO₂ (24–60% depending on the colour-coded adapter) — not the highest overall.
